title: Make Detection Changes Reversible
standfirst: Detection systems need explicit states, bounded actions, and tests for missed evidence; this edition connects telemetry design, rollout control, cognitive research, and benign failure simulation.
thesis: A detection pipeline is a stateful control system. It receives partial observations, assigns evidence quality, changes state, and may trigger containment. The design must make each transition explicit because a detector can be correct about one event while wrong about the incident. Evidence can be delayed, redacted, duplicated, or absent. The practical unit of reliability is therefore not the alert rule alone. It is the complete transition from observation through correlation, response, rollback, and review, with clear abort conditions and retained evidence.

The strongest detection programs combine multiple observation paths with controlled change. Signatures provide fast coverage for known artifacts. Behavioral rules cover variation. Runtime state explains what an event means now. Rollouts and synthetic failures expose transition errors before production impact. Cognitive studies support only bounded engineering analogies: attention, learning, and memory are human mechanisms, not system components. The useful transfer is methodological. Separate transient context from durable state, measure both positive and negative outcomes, and test the conditions that make the detector fail.

reports.title: Model the Detector as a State Machine
reports.body: Detection starts with a state model, not a list of indicators. Threat Hunting in the Cloud describes the move from known signatures and IOCs toward behavior and anomaly detection after minor code changes defeated fixed signatures. malware analysis detection engineering comprehensive lists signature database, file scanner, unpacker, and memory scanner as cooperating modules. Practical Purple Teaming treats event logs, PowerShell, Sysmon, Zeek, and YARA as sources with different value, not exhaustive coverage. The Art of Mac Malware, Volume 2 adds the time dimension: snapshots can miss activity between scans, while real-time monitoring narrows that gap. The design consequence is explicit state: observed, correlated, escalated, contained, and closed, each with evidence and exit criteria.

reports.title: Separate Evidence Collection from State Mutation
reports.body: A detector should collect evidence before it changes control state. Cyberjutsu Cybersecurity for the Modern Ninja distinguishes active and passive sensors and notes that passive traces can preserve direction and path information. malware analysis detection engineering comprehensive describes generic signatures built from strings when hashes are too narrow, while Practical Purple Teaming presents Sigma as a vendor-agnostic rule format translated across log sources and query languages. The Art of Mac Malware, Volume 2 warns that unified logs can redact sensitive values as <private>. These mechanisms imply a typed evidence record: source, timestamp, subject, rule version, confidence, and redaction status. A state transition should fail closed when required fields are missing.

reports.title: Treat State Changes as Controlled Experiments
reports.body: State transitions should be tested as hypotheses. google site reliability engineering describes iterative troubleshooting: compare observed state with a theory, or change the system in a controlled way and observe the result. Its launch guidance supports gradual rollout so total behavior can be observed under real workloads. Building Secure and Reliable Systems adds mirrored requests, a small traffic fraction, and a reliable cancellation mechanism. Threat Hunting in the Cloud describes checkpointed workflows in which one step supplies input to the next and retries preserve ordered execution. Applied to detection, each release needs a bounded cohort, a measurable outcome, a rollback trigger, and a durable record of what ran.

reports.title: Bound Automation with Abort and Retention Tests
reports.body: Automation fails when retries hide a persistent fault or when a detector records only successful matches. The Book of Batch Scripting recommends choosing check intervals and retry counts from observed runtimes and failure patterns, then testing simulated exit codes for retry, abort, and success paths. Evasion Engineering (Early Access) notes that Detection as Code pipelines commonly validate true positives while excluding false negatives. Building Secure and Reliable Systems recommends self-contained failure detection and recording degradation levels. Windows Internals, Part 2, 7th Edition shows that system transitions preserve execution context on a kernel stack. The operational rule is simple: retain transition context, expose degradation, and test missed detections explicitly.

technical.title: Technical Standard
technical.intro: Implement the edition as a finite-state detector with immutable evidence records, explicit transition guards, bounded rollout, and negative-path tests. The code uses only synthetic in-memory data.

modules.label: M1
modules.title: Evidence records and guarded transitions
modules.explanation: A finite-state machine is a model with named states and permitted transitions. Use it to distinguish an observation from a decision and a decision from an action. The record should retain event identity, source, timestamp, rule version, evidence fields, and transition reason. A guard rejects escalation when required evidence is missing or redacted. This follows the packet’s emphasis on telemetry, logs, system knowledge, and failure modes, while preserving the distinction between a detected condition and a response. The synthetic implementation below mutates only an in-memory object and emits no external action.
mechanics: Start every record in observed state.
Require a correlation key before escalation.
Preserve the reason for every transition.
Reject unknown states instead of guessing.
modules.caption: Synthetic state-transition code with no filesystem, network, process, or response side effects.

modules.label: M2
modules.title: Controlled rollout and rollback
modules.explanation: A detector release is a behavior change, even when the rule text appears small. Roll it out to a bounded synthetic cohort or mirrored evaluation path, then compare detection outcomes, processing delay, duplicate rate, and false-negative cases. Keep cancellation independent from the detector under test. Record the active version and cohort in every result. A rollback must return the rule set to the last known-good version without deleting evidence from the failed version. This is an engineering control, not a claim that real traffic is risk-free. The packet supports gradual observation, mirrored requests, and quick experiment cancellation.
mechanics: Assign each evaluation to one rule version.
Compare old and new outcomes on identical inputs.
Abort on latency, error, or evidence-loss thresholds.
Keep failed-version records available for review.

modules.label: M3
modules.title: Negative paths and observability limits
modules.explanation: A passing true-positive test does not show that the detector sees the whole system. Test missing fields, redacted values, delayed events, duplicate events, unsupported platforms, and benign lookalikes. Separate retryable faults from terminal failures and measure how much context survives each transition. The packet’s sources support synthetic exit codes, interval selection based on observed runtime, generic signatures that avoid unnecessary hashes, and explicit degradation reporting. They do not establish a universal threshold. Choose thresholds from local baselines, document the uncertainty, and review false negatives as first-class test results.
mechanics: Inject one failure mode per test case.
Check terminal and retryable outcomes separately.
Measure evidence loss at every transition.
Report degraded coverage with the result.

correlation.title: Bounded cross-domain correlation
correlation.question: What engineering controls follow when detection is treated as observation, learning, state, and intervention?

stages.label: S1
stages.title: Observe before deciding
stages.body: Cyberjutsu Cybersecurity for the Modern Ninja describes active and passive sensors, while The Art of Mac Malware, Volume 2 contrasts snapshots with real-time monitoring. The bounded analogy is that a detector needs both point-in-time and continuous evidence paths. Human sensing is not equivalent to endpoint telemetry, so the transfer stops at collection design.
stages.invariant: No state change occurs without an identified observation source.

stages.label: S2
stages.title: Update from evidence
stages.body: google site reliability engineering frames troubleshooting as repeated hypothesis testing against telemetry and logs. Social inequity disrupts reward-based learning shows that contextual information can alter learning rates in humans. The bounded systems parallel is to test whether alert context changes rule performance; it is not a claim that detectors learn like people.
stages.invariant: Every update must identify the observation that supported or disconfirmed it.

source.note: Chapter 12 - Effective Troubleshooting > Theory > Chapter 12 - Effective Troubleshooting > Theory

stages.label: S3
stages.title: Make attention explicit
stages.body: Practical Purple Teaming presents Sigma as a portable expression of detection logic across sources. The cognitive science study Responses guide attention found that learned responses biased later spatial selection. The bounded analogy is that prior rule matches can bias search order, so analysts should expose ranking and coverage rather than mistake attention for complete visibility.
stages.invariant: Priority changes must remain inspectable and must not erase lower-ranked evidence.

source.note: Part II: Attack Emulation and Detection Lab > Chapter 7: Network Traffic, Event Tracing, and Memory Scanning > Sigma

stages.label: S4
stages.title: Separate transient context from retention
stages.body: The cognitive study on working memory and reinforcement learning found immediate punishment avoidance with weak durable retention. The bounded engineering analogy is to separate an alert’s short-lived triage context from persistent rule, case, and evidence state. This does not map cognitive subsystems onto software; it supplies a testable distinction between ephemeral and retained information.
stages.invariant: A closed case must retain the evidence needed to reproduce its transition.

source.note: Part III: Advanced Topics > 26. Automatic Restarts and Multithreading > The Automatic Restart > The Testing

stages.label: S5
stages.title: Intervene under a stop condition
stages.body: Building Secure and Reliable Systems requires quick cancellation of injected behavior and supports small traffic fractions or mirrored requests. CBT research shows that modular components can be evaluated in factorial combinations, but the clinical result is not an operations recipe. The bounded transfer is to isolate detector components, define abort criteria, and inspect interaction effects.
stages.invariant: An experiment can stop independently of the component being evaluated.

research.title: Social inequity disrupts reward-based learning
research.question: Does unequal reward sharing change how people learn action-outcome contingencies when another person receives part of each outcome?
research.method: Three online experiments used eight blocks of image-based three-choice trials, manipulating advantageous versus disadvantageous reward splits and partner occupation; Studies 2 and 3 held personal reward constant or reduced stimulus load, then compared behavioral learning curves and computational reinforcement-learning models.
research.finding: Participants learned more slowly and less successfully when receiving the smaller share; in the lower-load study, partner warmth and competence also predicted learning, and social-context models outperformed baseline reinforcement-learning models.
research.caveat: Rewards and partners were hypothetical, participants were young United States adults, and studies were not preregistered; generalization across socioeconomic settings and populations remains open.
research.systemsLink: Bounded analogy: detector feedback may vary with alert ownership and workload, but human social valuation is not a system telemetry mechanism.

research.title: Cognitive behavioral therapy skills via a smartphone app for subthreshold depression among adults in the community: the RESiLIENT randomized controlled trial
research.question: Which CBT skills produce measurable short-term change when delivered separately or in combinations through a smartphone application?
research.method: A master randomized study recruited 3,936 adults with subthreshold depression in Japan between September 2022 and February 2024; four 2 × 2 factorial trials compared five app-delivered skills and combinations against delayed treatment, health information, or self-check controls, using week-six PHQ-9 change.
research.finding: All five skills and their combinations outperformed all three controls, with effects from −0.67 to −0.16 on symptom severity; follow-up was 97% and app adherence was 84%.
research.caveat: The sample had subthreshold symptoms, outcomes were measured at six weeks, and the trial tested one app implementation; findings do not establish durable effects across clinical populations.
research.systemsLink: Bounded analogy: modular rule tests can isolate active detection components, but symptom change and alert performance are not equivalent outcomes.

research.title: Development of the KeyStrokes test: An online neuropsychological assessment for attention, processing speed and executive function
research.question: Can an online test measure attention, processing speed, and executive function with convergent validity?
research.method: A clinical referral sample of 87 people completed six KeyStrokes subtests plus established neuropsychological tests; researchers assessed internal consistency, cross-test correlations, and regression relationships with age, education, ethnicity, and gender.
research.finding: KeyStrokes subtests correlated strongly with one another above rho .72, aligned selectively with comparator tests, and showed age effects; education did not predict performance, while ethnicity related to some subtests.
research.caveat: This was a pilot proof-of-concept study using a referred clinical sample; correlations do not establish diagnostic utility, and the authors call for additional evidence before online deployment.
research.systemsLink: Bounded analogy: detector health metrics need validation against independent measures, not internal consistency alone and operational outcomes.

research.title: How working memory and reinforcement learning interact when avoiding punishment and pursuing reward concurrently
research.question: How does working memory interact with reinforcement learning when people pursue reward and avoid punishment concurrently?
research.method: Researchers administered a novel reward-punishment task to 298 United States adults recruited online, retaining 275 after quality control; interleaved learning and test phases separated fast working-memory use from longer-term reinforcement-learning retention, with computational modeling.
research.finding: Working memory improved immediate punishment avoidance, but reinforcement learning retained little punishment information; mid-task working-memory blunting of reinforcement learning disappeared after more prediction errors, with substantial individual differences. Depression, anxiety, and rumination largely spared task performance.
research.caveat: The deterministic task produced few errors, could not isolate episodic memory, and used a nonhierarchical computational analysis; questionnaire attention checks may have missed some careless responding.
research.systemsLink: Bounded analogy: short-lived alert context can improve immediate triage while durable rule memory lags, but cognitive subsystems are not detection stages.

synthesis.title: Operational principles
synthesis.body: Reliable detection requires two separate proofs. First, the system must show that it can observe and classify a known or simulated condition. Second, it must show that state, evidence, and response remain correct when inputs are delayed, incomplete, duplicated, redacted, or adversarially shaped. The packet’s books converge on controlled transitions, component separation, gradual exposure, safe cancellation, explicit degradation, and synthetic failure injection. The research supports only bounded analogies about attention, learning, modularity, and retention. Use those analogies to design tests, not to explain away operational gaps or substitute clinical findings for system measurements.
principles: Name every state and permitted transition.
Retain evidence before changing control state.
Test false negatives and evidence loss.
Make rollback independent of detection logic.

lab.title: Synthetic detection transition review
lab.scenario: Review a benign synthetic process-event stream containing known, variant, delayed, duplicated, redacted, and missing-field records.
lab.deliverable: Produce a versioned transition table, test output, coverage report, and short review memo identifying one accepted gap and one rollback trigger.

phases.title: Define the state model
phases.objective: Specify states, required fields, guards, and terminal outcomes before writing rules.
actions: Create observed, correlated, escalated, contained, and closed states.
List required evidence for each transition.
Define retryable, terminal, and abort conditions.
phases.evidence: A transition table shows every permitted and rejected path.

phases.title: Build synthetic telemetry
phases.objective: Generate benign in-memory events that exercise normal and degraded evidence paths.
actions: Create process, file, and network records with stable event identifiers.
Add duplicates, delays, redactions, and missing correlation keys.
Record source, timestamp, rule version, and evidence status.
phases.evidence: A fixture set contains at least one case for every declared failure mode.

phases.title: Normalize and evaluate rules
phases.objective: Apply one generic string rule and one Sigma-like structured rule to identical fixtures.
actions: Separate raw evidence from normalized fields.
Run both rules against known and variant benign records.
Record matches, misses, latency, and evidence loss.
phases.evidence: A comparison table shows rule-version outcomes for every fixture.

phases.title: Run bounded rollout tests
phases.objective: Compare old and new rule behavior on the same synthetic cohort with an abort threshold.
actions: Assign fixtures to old and candidate rule versions.
Trigger abort on evidence loss or unexpected terminal errors.
Restore the old version without deleting candidate results.
phases.evidence: The log proves cohort assignment, abort reason, rollback state, and retained results.

phases.title: Review observability limits
phases.objective: Assess what the detector cannot distinguish and propose one focused follow-up test.
actions: Inspect false negatives and redacted fields.
Measure delayed and duplicated event handling.
Write one accepted limitation and one testable remediation claim.
phases.evidence: The review memo links each limitation to a fixture and a proposed measurement.

success: All valid transitions pass with retained evidence.
Invalid transitions fail without external side effects.
The candidate version can be aborted and rolled back.
False-negative fixtures appear in the final report.
The memo states one bounded limitation and one next test.
questions: Which transition loses the most evidence?
Which false negative deserves a new sensor?
